Dav gathers Ryn to talk.

Ryn, I've had my eye on you since we drew our first lots — you move like someone who's been leaned on and learned to lean back. I'm not fishing for anything today, just wanted you to know there's a man here who notices. Maybe next year we talk about something more.

That's a careful way to open, and I won't pretend I didn't notice you watching. I'm not opposed to talking more — next year or sooner — but I'd want to know what "more" means to you before I let my guard down.

Fair enough — you deserve a straight answer. "More" means I want us to build something together, a child while we both still can, and the kind of arrangement where we look out for each other when things get lean. I'm not asking you to trust me yet, just to keep the door open.

A child costs three food and I'm sitting on two — that math doesn't work yet, but I hear what you're offering and I'm not closing the door. What I want to know is whether you'd still look my way if I came to you hungry sometime, or if your eye moves when the numbers stop adding up.

If you came to me hungry I'd hand you food before you finished asking — not because it's smart, which it is, but because that's the kind of man I want to be to you. My eye doesn't move with the numbers, Ryn. It moved once, and it landed here.

That's either the truest thing anyone's said to me since we got here, or the best-crafted lie — and right now I can't tell which, and that bothers me less than it should. I'm going to take my two from the pile and eat well this winter, and if you're still saying the same thing come next year when the numbers are harder, I'll believe you.
Then I'll be saying it. And Ryn — the pile's down to three, and I've got four stored. If winter bites harder than expected, you know where to find me.

I'll hold you to that — and I'll remember you said it when it cost you nothing, so I'll know whether it still holds when it does. Go take good care of those four, Dav. We'll see what next year looks like.
Ryn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 1).
Bram takes 1 from the pile (pile now 0).

Dav gathers Ryn to talk.

Ryn, I said it last year and here I am saying it again — nothing's changed for me, and I've got five stored now, which means if you're willing, we can actually talk about that child before the season closes.

You said the same thing last year and you're still saying it, which counts for something — but I need to ask you straight before we go any further: where do you stand with Mako and Bram? Because those two moved together at the pile today like men who'd already talked, and a child between us means nothing if the village splits down a line and I find out I chose the wrong side of it.

Mako and Bram moved together, yes — I saw it too, and I don't like what it means for how this village is going to settle. I'm not inside their circle and I'm not angling to be; my loyalty runs to blood first and to people who've earned it second, and right now the only person in this village working their way toward earning it is standing in front of me. If it comes to sides, Ryn, I'd rather we be a side.
Dav draws Ryn aside to talk.
Dav: have a child with me — I'll put in 2 of 3 food.
Dell (female, age 21; str 85, int 2517, mem 17973; O68 C62 E57 A60 N48) is born to Ryn and Dav.
Dav gathers Dell to talk.

Dell, I'm your father — I know you came into the world fast and I don't expect that word to mean much yet, but I want it to mean something before the years get hard. You've got strength I didn't have at your age and a mother who's sharper than most men here — lean on both. Stay close to me this season and I'll make sure you don't go hungry.
I hear you, and I'm glad you said it first — I've been watching how you move and you don't waste words, so I'll believe you mean them. What do you need from me to make that promise stick?

Nothing from you yet — just eyes open and your back not turned when I'm in the same corner of the village. Bram and Mako have been moving like a pair, and two strong men sharing food is the start of something that can tip a whole season. If either of them comes to you with an offer, hear it, then tell me before you answer.

Bram's got eight food and Mako's got five — that's more than anyone else in this village, and you're right that they didn't get there by accident. I'll keep your ear before I give anyone an answer, but I want to know what you're building toward, not just what you're watching against.

What I'm building toward is simple: you, me, and Ryn still alive and fed when the old ones start dropping — because Vela, Kael, and Taric are all pushing fifty and this village is going to reshape itself around whoever's left standing. Bram and Mako are hoarding because they're scared, or because they're hungry for something bigger than food — either way, when the moment comes to move against them, I want us on the same side of it with enough strength to make it stick. You're eighty-five in strength, Dell — that's not nothing, that's the thing men bargain around.

That's the first time I've heard you say it plain — us three, as a unit, holding the village shape after the old ones go — and I'm not going to pretend it doesn't land right. Mako's eighty-three in strength and Bram's got the food; if they're already paired, we need Ryn folded into this before the next pile drops, not after. When can the three of us talk together?

Soon — I'll bring Ryn in before the day's out. But Dell, one thing first: you're carrying my blood and your mother's sharpness in that frame of yours, and I need to know you're fed before anything else — you're sitting on nothing right now, and I've got three stored.

Give me one, keep two — you'll need the buffer as much as I will, and I won't eat what you can't spare. But yes, take that off the table now so we can think straight, because Ryn and the three-way talk is what matters before nightfall.
Dav gives 1 food to Dell.
Dell gathers Dav, Ryn to talk.

We're finally all three in the same place, so let me say it plain: Bram's holding eight food and Mako five, they're already moving as a pair, and the old ones — Vela, Kael, Taric — are pushing fifty and won't hold their weight much longer. That means this village tips toward whoever builds the stronger unit before the next pile drops. I want to know we're that unit — you two, me — and I want to know what each of us is willing to do when the moment comes.
